title: Asset and Safehouse
premise: Rosalind Fairweather, a transport-safety investigator whose parents died in row twelve of Flight 4471, has spent seven years inside a system that keeps quietly rewriting its own rules. When her former handler — officially dead for two years — sends her a calendar invitation for tomorrow, she walks into a safehouse meeting already under surveillance and discovers a plot to destroy a passenger ferry and stage it as mechanical failure, implicating the very agency that buried the truth about row twelve. Racing a countdown she can't fully read, Rosalind must choose between handing the evidence to the institutions that betrayed her family and acting outside the law with the one person she was ordered never to trust. In the end she stops the attack at the cost of her career and her cover identity, inherits her handler's hidden archive, and chooses love and open truth over duty to a corrupted system.
about_author: Rafael Marchetti is a former maritime safety auditor who spent a decade writing incident reports no one read before turning to fiction. He lives near a working harbor, where he claims every foghorn sounds like a plot point.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Seven years after losing her parents on Flight 4471, Rosalind testifies at a safety hearing and watches regulators soften her findings into nothing. That night, grieving the futility, she receives a calendar invite from Marcus Hale — her old handler, dead for two years. Beat: quiet despair cracked open by impossible hope.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. She verifies the invite's cryptographic signature: genuinely Hale's, timestamped yesterday. Digging into his 'death,' she finds a closed file, a crematorium record with no body, and a note in his handwriting: 'Bring nothing. Trust the man from the pier.' Beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Man from the Pier
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. At a rain-soaked marina she meets Daniel Okafor, Hale's other asset — a disgraced coast guard officer who received the same invitation. They distrust each other instantly, bound only by a dead man's summons. Beat: wary alliance forged in mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: POV Daniel. Daniel leads Rosalind to Hale's abandoned safehouse, where they find a dead-drop protocol still running and a burner phone that rings at midnight. A voice gives them thirty seconds of instructions, then hangs up forever. Beat: dread — they are being steered by a ghost.

chapters.title: What Hale Buried
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Inside a wall cavity: Hale's private archive proving Flight 4471's 'pilot error' verdict was manufactured to protect a defense contractor, and a partial dossier on something called MERIDIAN — a staged disaster planned to look like equipment failure. Beat: grief transmuted into fury.

chapters.title: The Ferry Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Daniel. Cross-referencing MERIDIAN with port schedules, Daniel identifies the target: the Corvina Star, a passenger ferry sailing Thursday with 400 aboard, including a whistleblower who could expose the contractor. Beat: cold clarity — the accident has a date.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind takes the evidence to her agency mentor, Eleanor Voss, and watches Voss report her instead. Ordered to surrender the archive and stand down, Rosalind understands the institution will protect itself, not the passengers. Beat: betrayal; the last door inside the law closes.

chapters.title: Two Days
chapters.summary: POV Daniel. Daniel and Rosalind go dark, sheltering in a second safehouse while mapping the Corvina Star's crew and security. Between operational planning, an unguarded conversation reveals their parallel losses — his career, her family — and something tender begins. Beat: intimacy against duty.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. They locate Priya Nair, the engineer slated to die aboard, and convince her the 'routine inspection' clearing the ferry is a kill order. Priya confirms MERIDIAN's mechanism: a sabotaged fuel line designed to mimic corrosion. Beat: urgency compounds; a life added to the stakes.

chapters.title: Counter-Surveillance
chapters.summary: POV Daniel. A tail finds them; a chase through the old fish market ends with Daniel wounded and their safehouse burned. They realize the opposition isn't contractors alone — someone inside the agency is feeding MERIDIAN timelines. Beat: hunted, cornered, committed.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind confronts Voss privately and discovers Voss is playing a longer game: she reported Rosalind to buy credibility while assembling her own case against the contractor. Uneasy triangulation — three players, one truth, no trust. Beat: moral ambiguity deepens.

chapters.title: Hale's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: POV Daniel. Decoding the final layer of the archive, they find Hale alive until six weeks ago and a video message: he staged his death to finish MERIDIAN's investigation and chose them because they'd do what rules forbid. He names the insider. Beat: the ghost becomes a father figure; purpose crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Insider
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The traitor is Deputy Director Callum Reeve — the man who signed off on Flight 4471's false verdict. Confronting his record, Rosalind sees her family's crash and tomorrow's ferry are the same crime, seven years apart. Beat: personal and plot fuse into one wound.

chapters.title: Boarding Passes
chapters.summary: POV Daniel. With hours left, they plan boarding under Priya's inspector credentials. Voss offers official cover at a price: hand over Hale's archive afterward, no copies. Rosalind must decide whether justice requires trusting another institution. Beat: the theme made explicit — trust as wager.

chapters.title: Sailing Night
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. They board the Corvina Star at dusk, blending with four hundred passengers. Rosalind walks row twelve's equivalent — seat twelve on the aft deck — and lets herself feel the fear she's outrun for seven years. Beat: stillness before the storm; love confessed quietly between checks.

chapters.title: Fuel Line
chapters.summary: POV Daniel. In the engine room, Daniel and Priya find the sabotage installed and armed on a timer. Disabling it triggers a silent alarm; Reeve's team is already aboard, disguised as port security. Beat: the trap springs — stopping the bomb was never the whole mission.

chapters.title: Four Hundred Witnesses
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. To avoid a panic massacre, they can't evacuate openly; instead they trigger a genuine mechanical fault that forces an authorized return to port, emptying the ship legally. Reeve realizes he's been outmaneuvered by procedure itself. Beat: triumph through ingenuity, not force.

chapters.title: The Long Pier
chapters.summary: POV Daniel. As passengers disembark, Reeve's men corner Daniel on the pier. Outnumbered and bleeding, Daniel holds the dock long enough for the last families to clear the gangway. Beat: sacrifice offered; duty and love finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: Reeve
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind corners Reeve in the terminal's control room, recording his confession as he offers her everything — her family's truth, her career restored — for silence. She refuses and transmits live to Voss and the press. Beat: climax; justice chosen over every bargain.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Reeve is arrested; the contractor unravels; Flight 4471's file reopens. But the agency moves to seize Hale's archive, and Rosalind honors her word to Voss — except for one copy she keeps for the row twelve families. Beat: bittersweet cost accounting.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Daniel. Recovering in the safehouse, Daniel learns Hale left him the property and Rosalind the archive's stewardship — an inheritance not of money but of obligation. They decide to finish Hale's work independently, outside any badge. Beat: renewal; duty transformed into choice.

chapters.title: Tomorrow's Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Months later, Rosalind stands at the memorial wall where row twelve's names are carved, Daniel beside her. A new encrypted invitation arrives — from someone claiming to be Hale. She smiles, pockets the phone, and walks toward whatever comes next. Beat: resolution with an open horizon; love and vigilance together.
